statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail is 7% in the low band roughly 90 minutes into the Sunday Globex session.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. A narrow evidence-based danger window is flagged over the 13:00-15:00 UTC Monday window containing the U.S. cash open, where an opening-auction gap can extend before it retraces. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ accepts above 30,000 at 30,015 (+0.33%) after a two-way reopen; Tail edges to 7% while a 4.94% 10-year, $100 oil and a structurally closed Hormuz hold Stress at 34%
body: About ninety minutes into the Globex session the NQ price path is modestly higher and shallow. Futures print 30,015.00, up 97.75 points (+0.33%) against the 29,917.25 Friday settle, inside an observed 29,904.50-30,034.00 range; Investing.com's delayed feed corroborates at 30,016.00 (+0.33%). The important structural detail is that the low was set below the settle before the recovery, so discovery has been genuinely two-way, and the entire excursion spans 129.5 points, about 0.43%. Price now sits within roughly 19 points of the session high, which is a mild amplifier on its own, but it is a slow grind on a pre-Tokyo book rather than the persistent no-retracement extension that threatens a mean-reversion approach. Tail therefore edges only to 7%. The standing cash references remain Friday's triple-witching NDX close of 29,644.17 (+0.67%) and a VIX close of 14.81 (-4.08%), which leaves no volatility premium to unwind. The macro backdrop is unchanged and hawkish: the FOMC raised the target range a quarter point to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September on a unanimous 12-0 vote, the first increase since 2023, with one further increase penciled in for 2026. On Sunday, Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari said inflation is still too high in all aspects of the economy and goes well beyond oil, which is the first Fed input Asia can price. Rates remain the transmission channel, with the 10-year constant maturity last at 4.94% and the 2-year at 4.67%. Energy is elevated but stabilising, WTI near $100 and Brent near $104 after Friday's 1.58% decline, and the Strait of Hormuz remains structurally impaired at a small fraction of pre-crisis transits without any new escalation reported over the weekend. Internals into the weekend were narrow rather than uniformly strong, with semiconductor leadership set against divided megacaps and a majority of index members below their 20-day average, which argues for dispersion rather than index-level one-way structure. Stress accordingly holds at 34% in the moderate band, Confidence stays at 75% on a fresh, twice-corroborated live price path offset by weekend-stale volatility and yield references, and the mapped policy state remains EA_ON.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available and describe an unbroken low-Tail regime spanning the weekend halt and the Sunday reopen. Tail held between 4% and 6% in every hour, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout, while Stress drifted from 24% late on 19 September into a 30-34% band through Sunday as the post-hike rate backdrop and the elevated oil complex accumulated. Confidence ranged from 70% to 75%, dipping through the illiquid Sunday afternoon and recovering once the Globex reopen restored a live price path. Every hour was scored dominant mode normal, and nothing in the window recorded the persistent one-way structure that Tail measures.
outlookSummary: The cycle covers the remainder of the Asian session, the European session, and the Monday U.S. cash session through the 20:00 UTC close and into the Tuesday Globex reopen. Tail is projected to stay inside the low band in all 24 hours, so the mapped policy state remains EA_ON throughout. The projected peak is 12% in the hour containing the 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open, followed by 11% in the hour after it and 10% in the power hour into the close; the floor is 5% during the Globex maintenance halt, when no tradable path exists. Monday's scheduled calendar is light, carrying Fed Goolsbee at 10:30 UTC, the Chicago Fed National Activity Index at 12:30 UTC and routine bill auctions, so the main conditional risk is structural rather than event-driven: an opening auction that extends a gap before retracing. Confidence is projected to decay gradually from 75% to 66% as the live evidence gathered this hour ages.
